clue.text: Presume swimming is best

indicators.note: something swimming moves about in the water, so the letters drift into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, seven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone who presumes a swim is the finest thing going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Presume' reads as the verb of the sentence, but it is just the letters to be shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: Supreme describes the highest or greatest of its kind, a straight synonym for top quality.

clue.text: Emotional and regularly surly after very bad flu

indicators.note: after sets one piece behind the others in the line

parts.note: so means very, as in 'so good'

indicators.note: something bad has gone wrong, so the letters come out in a spoiled order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so take every other letter

parts.note: second and fourth letters of the word

explanation.surface: Someone gets weepy and grumpy while suffering from a nasty bout of flu.
explanation.walkthrough: SO plus a jumble of FLU gives SOULF, and the even letters of surly finish it off.
explanation.definitionFit: Soulful means expressing deep feeling, so it fits a description of being full of feeling.

clue.text: Legislator flying Martian airplane

indicators.note: flying things are tossed about through the air, so the letters land in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, fifteen letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A lawmaker piloting a spacecraft from Mars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flying' sits naturally with an airplane, which disguises its job of scrambling both words.
explanation.definitionFit: A parliamentarian is a member of a parliament, the body that makes laws, so a legislator.

clue.text: Group in goal is surrounded

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it, wrapped on both sides

parts.note: an end is an aim or purpose
a circle is a group of people, as in a circle of friends

explanation.surface: A squad of players crowded around the goalmouth.
explanation.walkthrough: Goal sounds like football, but here it is END in the sense of an aim.
explanation.definitionFit: Encircled means ringed on all sides, the same as being hemmed in or surrounded.

clue.text: Leaders of Eastern nations now usurping islands in the doldrums

indicators.note: leaders go at the front, so take the opening letter of each word

parts.note: first letters of these five words

explanation.surface: Eastern states seizing islands while their rivals are becalmed.
explanation.walkthrough: The political picture hides a simple run of initial letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the doldrums means feeling listless and bored, which is the weary state ennui names.

clue.text: Mediates now and then after Ant's partner lies

indicators.note: after places one piece behind the other

parts.note: Ant and Dec are a British TV presenting duo

indicators.note: now and then means at intervals, so keep every second letter

parts.note: even letters of the word

explanation.surface: A TV double act squabbling, with one presenter occasionally stepping in to make peace.
explanation.walkthrough: Ant and Dec are a famous British pair of television hosts, so Ant's partner is Dec.
explanation.definitionFit: Deceits are acts of deception or falsehood, so plural lies in the noun sense.

clue.text: Critic of French farm vehicle

parts.note: de is French for of
the classic farm vehicle

explanation.surface: Someone who disapproves of a French tractor.
explanation.walkthrough: Critic of French reads as a critic of France; instead the French word for of starts the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A detractor disparages or belittles someone, the role of a hostile critic.

clue.text: College organ is stuck

parts.note: C is the standard abbreviation for college
a lung is a breathing organ

explanation.surface: A college's pipe organ is jammed.
explanation.walkthrough: Organ in a college suggests the chapel instrument, but it is the body part.
explanation.definitionFit: Clung is the past tense of cling, meaning held on tightly or adhered, like being stuck.

clue.text: Wildly celebrating a hen or equivalent

indicators.note: wildly means without control, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written, fifteen letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A rowdy hen party, or something like it.
explanation.walkthrough: A hen here is a bride-to-be on her hen night, a British pre-wedding party; the words are just letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that are interchangeable can be swapped for each other, so they are equivalent in use.

clue.text: Confused after son put on piece of tack

indicators.note: after sets one piece behind the other in the line

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son
addled means muddled or confused

explanation.surface: A boy gets muddled after pinning on a drawing pin.
explanation.walkthrough: Tack suggests a small nail, but here it is horse equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: Tack is riding gear for horses, and the saddle is its main item, so fitting one is saddling.

clue.text: Scorn utter dunce ridiculously unwilling to accept change

indicators.note: something done ridiculously is absurd and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, fifteen letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Mocking a hopeless fool who stubbornly refuses to move with the times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Utter' looks like an adjective intensifying dunce, but all three opening words are anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Unreconstructed describes someone clinging to old views, having refused to modernise or reform.

clue.text: Father accepting story in leaflet

indicators.note: to accept is to take something in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title
a lie is a made-up story

explanation.surface: A priest agreeing to have his tale printed in a pamphlet.
explanation.walkthrough: Fr is the written title for a Catholic priest.
explanation.definitionFit: A flier is a printed sheet handed out for advertising, the same thing as a leaflet.

clue.text: Popular prophesy with a Latin opening

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
to augur is to foretell
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for Latin

explanation.surface: A well-liked forecast that begins with a Latin phrase.
explanation.walkthrough: Opening reads as a noun, but it is the adjective, as in an opening speech.
explanation.definitionFit: An inaugural event or speech is the first one, marking a beginning, so it is an opening.

clue.text: Green Day finding fame

parts.note: lime is a shade of green
day is the light hours, as opposed to darkness

explanation.surface: The punk band Green Day hitting the big time.
explanation.walkthrough: Green Day is an American rock band; split apart, the two words are clued separately.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the limelight means being the centre of public attention, so it stands for fame.

clue.text: Plant beginning to grow above ancient bar

indicators.note: in a down answer, what is above comes earlier in the line
a beginning is the start, so take just the first letter

parts.note: first letter of the word
olden means of old times
a rod is a bar or pole

explanation.surface: A plant starting to grow over an old pole.
explanation.walkthrough: Above only works as a placement in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Goldenrod is a tall perennial with yellow flower spikes, an example of a plant.

clue.text: Louse lay low behind a piano

indicators.note: behind sets one piece after the others

parts.note: taken as written
p is the musical marking for piano, softly
to lie low is to hide

explanation.surface: A cad hiding behind a piano.
explanation.walkthrough: Louse sounds like an insult for a rotten person, but it is the insect sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Aphids are known as plant lice, so a louse in the gardener's sense.

clue.text: Exhibition spaces moving opening down to get reactions

indicators.note: the first letter is shifted further down the word, a rearrangement of a single letter

parts.note: galleries are rooms or buildings for displaying art

explanation.surface: Galleries rehanging their opening show lower down to provoke a response.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the G moves: from first place to sixth, the rest stay put.
explanation.definitionFit: Allergies are the body's adverse responses to substances like pollen, so immune reactions.

clue.text: Coloured single old penny with bit of tallow

indicators.note: a bit is a small part, so keep just the first letter

parts.note: first letter of the word
one is a single thing
d was the symbol for a penny in Britain's pre-1971 currency

explanation.surface: An old coin dyed with a smear of animal fat.
explanation.walkthrough: The tallow letter goes first even though it comes last in the clue; with lets it sit anywhere. Old British pennies were written d.
explanation.definitionFit: Toned means tinted or given a particular shade, as in sepia-toned, so coloured.

clue.text: Jerk holding fliers following vehicles

indicators.note: to hold something is to grip it inside, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: a tic is an involuntary twitch
the Royal Air Force, Britain's air force
f is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

explanation.surface: An idiot holding up airmen who are tailing a convoy.
explanation.walkthrough: Jerk suggests an idiot, but it is a twitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Traffic is the collective name for cars and lorries moving on roads, so vehicles.

clue.text: Wishes to cross road left by independent young peers

indicators.note: to cross something is to stretch over it, so one piece spans the other

parts.note: to long is to wish
Rd is the abbreviation for road
L is the abbreviation for left
I is the abbreviation for independent

explanation.surface: Wanting to cross a road abandoned by some independent young aristocrats.
explanation.walkthrough: Wishes is the verb, giving LONGS, which straddles the three abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: A lordling is a minor or young lord, and lords are members of the peerage.

clue.text: Throw sterling to get unscrupulous lawyer

parts.note: to shy is to toss, as at a coconut shy
ster. is a dictionary abbreviation for sterling

explanation.surface: Tossing pounds about to hire a crooked lawyer.
explanation.walkthrough: Sterling is British money; its short form ster. is less familiar than stg.
explanation.definitionFit: Shyster is informal American slang for a disreputable professional, especially a crooked attorney.

clue.text: Knowledge of new areas being developed by South

indicators.note: to develop something is to work it into a different shape, so the letters change order

parts.note: taken as written, letters to rearrange
S is the abbreviation for south

explanation.surface: Learning about new zones being built up in the south of a region.
explanation.walkthrough: The South letter is added after the rearranged pair of words.
explanation.definitionFit: Awareness is the state of knowing about or perceiving something, close to knowledge.

clue.text: Top of limb lost in some smouldering remains

indicators.note: the top is the first letter in a down light, and it is the part to go
something lost is gone, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: a member is a limb of the body

explanation.surface: An arm or leg lost among the smoking ashes.
explanation.walkthrough: Limb gives MEMBER; dropping its first letter leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An ember is a glowing fragment left in a dying fire, part of what remains smouldering.

clue.text: Cut corners, putting top of mattress in refuse container

indicators.note: putting one thing in another places it inside

parts.note: in Britain a skip is a large open rubbish bin left on a street, like a dumpster

indicators.note: the top is the start, so keep only the first letter

parts.note: first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Saving effort by dumping an old mattress in a skip.
explanation.walkthrough: A skip is the British word for a builder's rubbish container.
explanation.definitionFit: To skimp is to economise by doing too little, which is what cutting corners means.

clue.text: High-sounding buck returns unknown

indicators.note: to return is to go back the way you came, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: a buck is a male deer
y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: A pompous dollar comes back as an unknown quantity.
explanation.walkthrough: High-sounding suggests pompous, but here it describes a thin, high voice.
explanation.definitionFit: A reedy voice or tone is thin and shrill, like a reed instrument, so high-pitched in sound.

clue.text: Flighty individual and female liberationist sent finally by one to gallows

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for female
a libber is a campaigner for liberation, as in women's libber

indicators.note: finally points to the end, so keep only the last letter

parts.note: last letter of the word
I is the Roman numeral one
a gibbet is a gallows

explanation.surface: A feather-brained feminist campaigner sent to be hanged.
explanation.walkthrough: Libber is informal for a liberation activist; a gibbet is a gallows-like structure.
explanation.definitionFit: A flibbertigibbet is a frivolous, scatterbrained person who chatters too much, someone flighty.

clue.text: Concentrated on coin colour

parts.note: a cent is a small coin
red is a colour

explanation.surface: Someone focused intently on the colour of a coin.
explanation.walkthrough: Concentrated on reads as one phrase, but on just links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Centred means focused on a single point, so effort that is centred is concentrated.

clue.text: Regret about following former chemist

indicators.note: following places this piece after the other

parts.note: past means former, as in past president

indicators.note: about can mean turned round, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: Sorrow over leaving a previous job at the pharmacy.
explanation.walkthrough: Chemist suggests a British pharmacist, but here it is a famous scientist.
explanation.definitionFit: Louis Pasteur was a French scientist known for pasteurisation and vaccines, a celebrated chemist.
